Let
\[
F(\lambda,\tau)=\lambda+a+(c\lambda+b)e^{-\lambda\tau}.
\]
At \(\tau=0\),
\[
F(\lambda,0)=(1+c)\lambda+(a+b),
\]
so the single characteristic root is
\[
\lambda=-\frac{a+b}{1+c}<0.
\]
Thus stability can change only when a characteristic root crosses the imaginary axis.

Put \(\lambda=i\omega\), \(\omega>0\), and write \(\theta=\omega\tau\). Then
\[
i\omega+a+(ic\omega+b)(\cos\theta-i\sin\theta)=0.
\]
Separating real and imaginary parts gives
\[
a+b\cos\theta+c\omega\sin\theta=0,
\]
\[
\omega+c\omega\cos\theta-b\sin\theta=0.
\]
Solving these two linear equations for \(\cos\theta,\sin\theta\),
\[
\cos\theta=-\frac{ab+c\omega^2}{b^2+c^2\omega^2},
\qquad
\sin\theta=\frac{\omega(b-ac)}{b^2+c^2\omega^2}.
\]
Since \(0<a<b\) and \(0<c<1\), we have \(b-ac>0\), so \(\sin\theta>0\). Hence the relevant angle lies in \((\pi/2,\pi)\).

The identity \(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1\) gives
\[
c^2(1-c^2)\omega^4+
\bigl(b^2(1-2c^2)+a^2c^2\bigr)\omega^2
-b^2(b^2-a^2)=0.
\]
This quadratic in \(\omega^2\) has exactly one positive root, because its leading coefficient is positive and its constant term is negative. Define \(\Omega>0\) by
\[
\Omega^2=
\frac{
-\bigl(b^2(1-2c^2)+a^2c^2\bigr)
+\sqrt{\bigl(b^2(1-2c^2)+a^2c^2\bigr)^2
+4c^2(1-c^2)b^2(b^2-a^2)}
}
{2c^2(1-c^2)}.
\]
Then the imaginary-axis crossings occur exactly at
\[
\tau_k=\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{\Omega},
\qquad k=0,1,2,\dots,
\]
where \(\theta\in(\pi/2,\pi)\) is determined by
\[
\cos\theta=-\frac{ab+c\Omega^2}{b^2+c^2\Omega^2},
\qquad
\sin\theta=\frac{\Omega(b-ac)}{b^2+c^2\Omega^2}.
\]

It remains to check the crossing direction. Differentiating \(F(\lambda,\tau)=0\) implicitly,
\[
\frac{d\lambda}{d\tau}
=
\frac{\lambda(c\lambda+b)e^{-\lambda\tau}}
{1+ce^{-\lambda\tau}-\tau(c\lambda+b)e^{-\lambda\tau}}.
\]
At \(\lambda=i\Omega\), using the crossing equations, one obtains
\[
\operatorname{Re}\frac{d\lambda}{d\tau}
\quad\text{has the sign of}\quad
\Omega(1+c\cos\theta)+ac\sin\theta.
\]
But the imaginary-part equation gives
\[
\Omega(1+c\cos\theta)=b\sin\theta,
\]
so
\[
\Omega(1+c\cos\theta)+ac\sin\theta=(b+ac)\sin\theta>0.
\]
Thus each crossing moves roots from the left half-plane into the right half-plane as \(\tau\) increases.

Since all roots are initially stable at \(\tau=0\), stability holds precisely before the first crossing.

Therefore the required delays are
\[
\boxed{
0<\tau<
\frac1{\Omega}
\arccos\!\left(
-\frac{ab+c\Omega^2}{b^2+c^2\Omega^2}
\right)
}
\]
where
\[
\boxed{
\Omega^2=
\frac{
-\bigl(b^2(1-2c^2)+a^2c^2\bigr)
+\sqrt{\bigl(b^2(1-2c^2)+a^2c^2\bigr)^2
+4c^2(1-c^2)b^2(b^2-a^2)}
}
{2c^2(1-c^2)}
}.
\]
